newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends flat on late dollar sale.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends flat on late dollar sale.

text.p: The Mexican peso recouped ground lost to the dollar to close unchanged on Monday as local dealers sold dollars in late trade after a session overshadowed by shifting U.S. long bond yields, traders said.
"The market was quiet...dealers are waiting for (U.S. housing starts) data tomorrow," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both ended unchanged at 7.9680/7.9720 and 7.9620/7.9690 per dollar, respectively.
Same-day peso contracts earlier ended 2.6 centavos weaker at 7.9825/7.9860 per dollar.
"The U.S. bond and stock markets are both weak, so I don't know why people sold dollars down here," another trader said.

"It was mainly one big bank that stepped in to sell." U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds pared an earlier fall, but still closed off 6/32 to yield 6.96 percent when the foreign exchange market closed in Mexico.
The Dow Jones was off 0.68 percent at 6,888.26 points in late trade.
Dealers also expressed surprise at the peso's recovery as money market traders were predicting slight falls in short-term primary rates at Tuesday night's auction.
